acquisition method: data dependent neutral loss triggered ETD (DDNL), decision tree (DT)

A data dependent neutral loss triggered ETD (DDNL) acquisition method in which every precursor is fragmented by CID and if a characteristic neutral loss of phosphoric acid is observed, the same precursor is also triggered for ETD analysis. We compared this DDNL strategy to the decision tree method developed by Coon and co-workers
alkylation reagent: cysteine alkylation was performed in situ with iodoacetamide
cleavage agent: proteins were digested with Trypsin Gold (Promega)
enrichment method: Two acquisition strategies were employed to identify phosphopeptides from IMAC enriched P. falciparum phosphopeptide samples.
fragmentation method: subjected to either CID or ETD fragmentation in the linear ion trap
instrument: coupled to an LTQ Orbitrap Velos hybrid mass spectrometer (Thermo Scientific)
ionization type: equipped with a nanospray ion source
labeling: We also performed proteome profiling experiments from schizont digests (starting material that was used for phosphorylation analysis) using direct LC–MS/MS analyses
reduction reagent: Parasite pellets were re-suspended in extraction buffer (4% SDS, 0.1 M DTT, 0.1 M Tris pH 8, 0.5 mM PMSF, 2 μg/ml Aprotinin/Leupeptin, 20 μM ZnCl and 25 mM Sodium fluoride)
reduction concentration: extraction buffer (4% SDS, 0.1 M DTT, 0.1 M Tris pH 8, 0.5 mM PMSF, 2 μg/ml Aprotinin/Leupeptin, 20 μM ZnCl and 25 mM Sodium fluoride)
